<description>
### Why

`building-on` in `contrib/guix/toolchains.scm` reads `(%current-system)` once, when the module is loaded. `guix shell` loads the manifest before it applies `--system`, so the value is the system of the machine that runs the build, not the system that Guix builds for.

So a build with `ADDITIONAL_GUIX_ENVIRONMENT_FLAGS="--system=aarch64-linux"` on an x86_64 machine (for example with `qemu-binfmt-service-type`, to get an aarch64 build machine) configures the aarch64 cross toolchain with `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu`. `gcc-cross-sans-libc` then fails to configure:

```
checking for CET support... configure: error: compiler and assembler with CET support are required for --enable-cet
```

### What changes

`building-on` becomes a procedure, and its three call sites call it. Guix then computes the triplet for each derivation, under the system that the derivation is built for.

### How I checked

- On master, `HOST=x86_64-linux-gnu guix shell -n --system=aarch64-linux -m contrib/guix/linux_static.scm` (with `toolchains.scm` on the load path, as `guix-build` does) gives `gcc-cross-sans-libc` with `--build=x86_64-guix-linux-gnu`. With this PR it gives `--build=aarch64-guix-linux-gnu`. That is the same derivation that `guix build -d --system=aarch64-linux` gives on master.
- Native builds (no `--system`): the toolchain derivations from `linux_static.scm` and `manifest_gui.scm` are identical on master and with this PR. So this PR does not change release builds.
- With this PR, an emulated aarch64 build of `x86_64-linux-gnu` on x86_64 built the whole cross toolchain and the non-GUI binaries. The GUI environment then failed in the tests of `python-pylint` (timeout under emulation) and `maturin` (snapshot mismatch). These packages have no aarch64 substitutes at the pinned Guix commit, and the failures are not related to this change.
</description>

building-on read %current-system when toolchains.scm was loaded. guix
shell loads the manifest before it applies --system, so a
--system=aarch64-linux build on an x86_64 machine configured the aarch64
